The initiative began as a collaborative effort to create transparent metrics that could be used by shippers for making informed decisions based not only on cost but also on sustainability criteria. Initially formed through discussions between key stakeholders in the Baltic Sea region—an area with significant maritime activity—the network has since expanded globally, reflecting its broader appeal and relevance. Its primary goal is simple yet impactful: to facilitate better environmental practices within ocean freight by providing reliable data that shippers can use when choosing their carriers. The BICEPS Network achieves this through a scoring system which assesses various sustainability parameters such as fuel efficiency, Emissions output (including CO2), noise levels and more recent additions like alternative fuels usage. texts.full_text: a Taxi Love in a Taxi is a 1980 American film starring Diane Sommerfield and Jim Jacobs. Plot The story of a romance between a Jewish New York cab driver, Sam, and Corinne, an African-American mother and bank clerk with a young son, Davey. After Davey rides in Sam's cab one day, Davey brings Sam and Corinne together. Corinne and Sam are accidentally involved in a drug scam that could land them both in serious trouble. Background Star Jim Jacobs had previously worked under director Robert Sickinger at the Hull House Association in Chicago during the 1970s, a community organization that worked to improve the lives of underprivileged residents in Chicago. This background in community work and social issues likely influenced Jacobs' performance and the director Robert Sickinger's approach to the film, which tackles themes of interracial relationships and social injustice in 1970s New York City. The film's setting and themes reflect the social and cultural dynamics of the time, including the ongoing civil rights movement and the challenges faced by interracial couples in a society still grappling with segregation and prejudice. The inclusion of a young, African-American son in the story, Davey, adds a layer of complexity, as the film explores the impact of interracial relationships on the next generation

In order to quantify the amount of unbound CarP Ab in the sample, a HRP-conjugated anti-human secondary antibody was added to each well to bind the immobilized CarP. After incubation, plate was washed to remove all unbound components. Then, HRP substrate was added for a short incubation period. A database of 255 patients who underwent microdecompression surgery by a single orthopedic spine surgeon between 2014 and 2018 was queried. Patients who underwent primary single-level ULBD of the lumbar spine were included. Visual analog scale (VAS) for back pain and leg pain and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) results were collected preoperatively and at 12 and 24 months postoperatively. Demographic, radiographic, and operative factors were assessed for associations with failure to improve. Clinically important improvement was defined as a decrease of at least 30% in both back pain VAS score and shoulder ache VAS score, or an Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score increase by more than 45%. Outcomes were conducted using mixed-effect regression models to account for repeated measures within individual patients. The analysis showed that multiple variables significantly predicted significant clinical improvement at both three and three months postoperatively: age over 70, preoperative ODI scores above a specific threshold indicating severe illness, female gender (though this association was not statistically meaningful), the absence of bilateral knee discomfort prior to surgery as shown by a lower baseline VAS score for shoulder trauma. The polyoxyalkylene backbones of the ASA capped compounds consist predominantly, if not exclusively, of repeating oxyethyl units (i.e., --O--CH2- CH3). These polymers are prepared by reacting ethoxyllated alcohols or amines with an aldehydic component. The end groups on these polyoxyalkylene chains carry the acryloyloctadecyldimethylphosphonium (ASA) group. The ASAs themselves consist of four components: 1-octanoyl, N,N-dialkylethanolamine, acrylic acid or its derivative and phosphonic acids. The presence in these colorants of a polyoxyalkylene chain allows them to be worked into the wax matrix without segregating out. The ASA group renders each molecule polarizable such that it will migrate within itself instead of spreading onto substrates like skin, other surfaces, or even hardened crayon waxes. Moreover these colorants are stable over time and temperature exposure in hot temperatures (e.g., above 40.degree.C.). This stability is achieved through the lower reactivity profile associated with ASAs compared to conventional pigments. The presence of this polyoxyalkylene chain also allows for easy handling, which has been a problem when using powders or dusts.
